question: A 24-year-old professional soccer player presents to the clinic with discomfort and pain while walking. He says that he has an unstable knee joint that started after an injury during a match last week. He adds that he heard a popping sound at the time of the injury. Physical examination of the knee reveals swelling of the knee joint with a positive anterior drawer test. Which of the following structures is most likely damaged in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Unstable knee joint after injury" -> "Popping sound heard during injury" -> "Swelling of the knee joint" -> "Positive anterior drawer test" -> "Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) most likely damaged" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Positive anterior drawer test" -> "Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) most likely damaged" -> 90%
analysis: Based on the history of a popping sound at the time of injury, swelling, and a positive anterior drawer test, the most likely structure damaged in this patient is the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The ACL is commonly injured during activities that involve sudden stops or changes in direction, such as in soccer.
